name: sand3d
description: 3D modeling in Python, built for LLMs.
readmeExcerpt:
sand3d

**3D modeling in Python, built for LLMs.** sand3d is a Python library for writing 3D objects as short programs: profiles, solids, edits, frames, joints and assemblies, over Blender's `bpy`. A program says *how* a shape is made, part by part and in its own words, so a model writes it in a few hundred tokens and a person can read it.

 Website ·  Docs ·  Datasets ·  Explorer

## Why sand3d


How it is measured, part by part

- **Short.** A part takes 2 to 6× fewer tokens than the same part in Blender Python, CadQuery or FeatureScript ([details](https://sand3d.sandflow.ai/tokens.html)). - **The whole API fits in a prompt**, about 3,600 tokens ([the API](https://sand3d.sandflow.ai/api.html)). - **Named, not computed.** Parts, edges and faces are reached by name, never by hand-computed coordinates. - **Deterministic.** The same program builds the same mesh, bit for bit. ## A whole object, part by part

A front-loading washing machine in 38 lines of code ([play it and read it](https://sand3d.sandflow.ai/gallery.html)): the cabinet, the drum, the door with its glass and handle, the detergent drawer and the dial, each a named part, and four joints that say how they move. ```python door = s3d.group("door", ring, glass, handle) # the handle and the glass move with it s3d.joint("door_hinge", door, hinge, axis="-Z", range=(0, 143)) s3d.joint("drum_spin", drum, front.move(0, 400), kind="continuous") s3d.joint("drawer_slide", drawer, top_band.move(150), kind="prismatic", axis="+X", range=(0, 200)) s3d.joint("dial_turn", dial, top_band.move(-150), kind="continuous") return s3d.assembly("washing_machine", cab, drum, door, drawer, dial, front=front) ``` ## Export: GLB, URDF, USD, OBJ, STL One call; the file's extension names the format; lengths in metres. ```python s3d.export(machine, "washer.glb") # or .urdf, .usda, .obj, .stl ``` | format | what it carries | for | |---|---|---| | **GLB** | meshes, materials, the joints in each node's extras, at the current pose | the web, viewers, game engines | | **URDF** | a link per moving part, its joints and their limits, at rest; OBJ meshes beside it | ROS, PyBullet, MuJoCo, Isaac | | **USDA** | the same tree in OpenUSD (UsdGeom, UsdPhysics), with the materials | Omniverse, Isaac Sim, USD pipelines | | **OBJ**, **STL** | the meshes alone, at the current pose: OBJ Y up, binary STL Z up | any 3D tool, slicers | `.usd`, `.usdc` and `.usdz` come from the `.usda` through USD's own tools (`usdcat`, `usdzip`). The scene is also an ordinary Blender scene, for anything else Blender writes. ## Install Python 3.13 (recommended) or 3.11. Blender comes with it, as the `bpy` module: 5.2 LTS on Python 3.13, 4.5 LTS on Python 3.11; CI runs bpy 5.2. ```bash pip install sand3d # or, in a uv project: uv add sand3d ``` `bpy` has no wheel for Python 3.12, nor for Intel Macs from 5.2 on: there, use Python 3.11. ## A first program ```python import sand3d as s3d def bracket(w=80, d=40, t=6, hole_d=6.6, pitch=50): plate = s3d.extrude("plate", s3d.rect(w, d, r=4), t) s3d.hole(plate, hole_d, on=s3d.grid(2, 1, pitch, 0)) s3d.fillet(plate, 1, edges="top") return plate s3d.export(bracket(), "bracket.glb") ``` Millimetres by default. Every verb with code that runs and its render: [the quickstart](https://sand3d.sandflow.ai/quickstart.html); objects to play joint by joint: [the gallery](https://sand3d.sandflow.ai/gallery.html); every signature: [the API](https://sand3d.sandflow.ai/api.html). The programs themselves: [docs/examples/](https://github.com/Sandflow-ai/sand3d/tree/main/docs/examples/) and [programs/](https://github.com/Sandflow-ai/sand3d/tree/main/programs/). ## Give it to your LLM Put [docs/api.md](https://github.com/Sandflow-ai/sand3d/blob/main/docs/api.md) in the system prompt: the rules of the vocabulary, every signature, and worked examples, in about 3 600 tokens; [llms.txt](https://github.com/Sandflow-ai/sand3d/blob/main/llms.txt) points a model at it. For objects of several parts, [the guidelines](https://sand3d.sandflow.ai/guidelines.html) give the eight rules of an assembly program: the plan first, then the details, then the parts. ## What is in it Everything on one flat `s3d.` surface: | family | verbs | |---|---| | profiles | `rect` `circle` `slot` `polygon` `poly` `arc` `spline` `superellipse` `text` `offset` `stroke` … (16) | | solids and paths | `extrude` `revolve` `sweep` `loft` `wire` `helix` `box` `cylinder` `tube` `sphere` `torus` `dome` … (15) | | edits | `cut` `join` `intersect` `split` `hole` `pocket` `fillet` `chamfer` `shell` `dent` … (15) | | frames and placement | `Frame` `face` `edge` `bbox` `local` `at` `transform` `grid` `ring` `along` `snap` | | articulation | `joint` `pose` `seat` | | assembly | `group` `assembly` `attach` `export` `units` `fingerprint` … (8) | | parts and materials | `gear` `knurl` `thread` `material` | No category verbs (`chair()`, `table()`): a category is a program written *in* sand3d. ## Datasets sand3d programs for five sources of 3D objects, on Hugging Face under CC BY 4.0.

sand3d-objaverse · Objaverse
Everyday objects from Objaverse, each rebuilt as a program.
sand3d-cad · CAD
Mechanical parts from public CAD models.
sand3d-articraft · Articraft
Articulated objects from Articraft, their joints declared.

sand3d-simready · SimReady
Simulation-ready assets from NVIDIA SimReady.
sand3d-automate · AutoMate
Mechanical assemblies from AutoMate, each part a function of its program.
Browse them in [the explorer](https://huggingface.co/spaces/Sandflow/sand3d-explorer), or all five in [the collection](https://huggingface.co/collections/Sandflow/sand3d-6aec268fbdcd3bc174236168). ## Citation If you use sand3d in your work, please cite it. `CITATION.cff` holds the same, and GitHub shows it as "Cite this repository". ```bibtex @misc{sand3d2026, author = {Neveu, Thibault and Loy, Andr{\'e}a}, title = {sand3d}, year = {2026}, note = {Version 1.6.3}, url = {https://github.com/Sandflow-ai/sand3d} } ``` ## Contributing and license How the library is built, tested and versioned: [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/Sandflow-ai/sand3d/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). Apache License 2.0: see [LICENSE](https://github.com/Sandflow-ai/sand3d/blob/main/LICENSE).

sand3d

3D modeling in Python, built for LLMs.

sand3d is a Python library for writing 3D objects as short programs: profiles, solids, edits, frames, joints and assemblies, over Blender's bpy. A program says how a shape is made, part by part and in its own words, so a model writes it in a few hundred tokens and a person can read it.

 Website ·  Docs ·  Datasets ·  Explorer

Why sand3d


How it is measured, part by part

  • Short. A part takes 2 to 6× fewer tokens than the same part in Blender Python, CadQuery or FeatureScript (details).
  • The whole API fits in a prompt, about 3,600 tokens (the API).
  • Named, not computed. Parts, edges and faces are reached by name, never by hand-computed coordinates.
  • Deterministic. The same program builds the same mesh, bit for bit.

A whole object, part by part

A front-loading washing machine in 38 lines of code (play it and read it): the cabinet, the drum, the door with its glass and handle, the detergent drawer and the dial, each a named part, and four joints that say how they move.

door = s3d.group("door", ring, glass, handle)                      # the handle and the glass move with it
s3d.joint("door_hinge", door, hinge, axis="-Z", range=(0, 143))
s3d.joint("drum_spin", drum, front.move(0, 400), kind="continuous")
s3d.joint("drawer_slide", drawer, top_band.move(150), kind="prismatic", axis="+X", range=(0, 200))
s3d.joint("dial_turn", dial, top_band.move(-150), kind="continuous")
return s3d.assembly("washing_machine", cab, drum, door, drawer, dial, front=front)

Export: GLB, URDF, USD, OBJ, STL

One call; the file's extension names the format; lengths in metres.

s3d.export(machine, "washer.glb")    # or .urdf, .usda, .obj, .stl
format what it carries for
GLB meshes, materials, the joints in each node's extras, at the current pose the web, viewers, game engines
URDF a link per moving part, its joints and their limits, at rest; OBJ meshes beside it ROS, PyBullet, MuJoCo, Isaac
USDA the same tree in OpenUSD (UsdGeom, UsdPhysics), with the materials Omniverse, Isaac Sim, USD pipelines
OBJ, STL the meshes alone, at the current pose: OBJ Y up, binary STL Z up any 3D tool, slicers

.usd, .usdc and .usdz come from the .usda through USD's own tools (usdcat, usdzip). The scene is also an ordinary Blender scene, for anything else Blender writes.

Install

Python 3.13 (recommended) or 3.11. Blender comes with it, as the bpy module: 5.2 LTS on Python 3.13, 4.5 LTS on Python 3.11; CI runs bpy 5.2.

pip install sand3d        # or, in a uv project: uv add sand3d

bpy has no wheel for Python 3.12, nor for Intel Macs from 5.2 on: there, use Python 3.11.

A first program

import sand3d as s3d

def bracket(w=80, d=40, t=6, hole_d=6.6, pitch=50):
    plate = s3d.extrude("plate", s3d.rect(w, d, r=4), t)
    s3d.hole(plate, hole_d, on=s3d.grid(2, 1, pitch, 0))
    s3d.fillet(plate, 1, edges="top")
    return plate

s3d.export(bracket(), "bracket.glb")

Millimetres by default. Every verb with code that runs and its render: the quickstart; objects to play joint by joint: the gallery; every signature: the API. The programs themselves: docs/examples/ and programs/.

Give it to your LLM

Put docs/api.md in the system prompt: the rules of the vocabulary, every signature, and worked examples, in about 3 600 tokens; llms.txt points a model at it. For objects of several parts, the guidelines give the eight rules of an assembly program: the plan first, then the details, then the parts.

What is in it

Everything on one flat s3d.<verb> surface:

family verbs
profiles rect circle slot polygon poly arc spline superellipse text offset stroke … (16)
solids and paths extrude revolve sweep loft wire helix box cylinder tube sphere torus dome … (15)
edits cut join intersect split hole pocket fillet chamfer shell dent … (15)
frames and placement Frame face edge bbox local at transform grid ring along snap
articulation joint pose seat
assembly group assembly attach export units fingerprint … (8)
parts and materials gear knurl thread material

No category verbs (chair(), table()): a category is a program written in sand3d.

Datasets

sand3d programs for five sources of 3D objects, on Hugging Face under CC BY 4.0.

Everyday objects from Objaverse, each rebuilt as a program.
sand3d-cad · CAD
Mechanical parts from public CAD models.
sand3d-articraft · Articraft
Articulated objects from Articraft, their joints declared.

Simulation-ready assets from NVIDIA SimReady.

Mechanical assemblies from AutoMate, each part a function of its program.

Browse them in the explorer, or all five in the collection.

Citation

If you use sand3d in your work, please cite it. CITATION.cff holds the same, and GitHub shows it as "Cite this repository".

  author = {Neveu, Thibault and Loy, Andr{\'e}a},

releases.name: sand3d 1.6.3
releases.body:
### Fixes

* A GLB holds only the root's tree, in metres: the rest of the scene no longer comes
  along, and a placed or mirrored root keeps its offset and its mirror (#11, fixes #10)

Thanks to @alaabenfatma for the report and the fix.

Install: `pip install sand3d` · Website: https://sand3d.sandflow.ai/

releases.name: sand3d 1.6.1
releases.body:
First public release of sand3d: profiles, solids, edits, frames, joints and an
assembly layer over Blender's `bpy`, with export to GLB, URDF, USD (`.usda`,
UsdPhysics), OBJ and STL. `pip install sand3d` brings the `bpy` its Python takes:
bpy 4.5 on Python 3.11, bpy 5.2 on Python 3.13. The API is described in
[docs/api.md](docs/api.md).

Install: `pip install sand3d` · Website: https://sand3d.sandflow.ai/

aiSummary.oneLiner: Toolkit for generating and manipulating 3D models using AI.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Sand3d provides tools and pipelines for integrating generative AI models with 3D workflows. It facilitates the conversion of text prompts or 2D images into textured 3D assets. The project handles mesh generation, UV mapping, and texture synthesis. It aims to accelerate asset creation for game development and virtual reality. The toolkit can be integrated into existing DCC applications like Blender.
keyFeatures: Text-to-3D generation: creates initial 3D meshes from descriptive text prompts.
Image-to-3D conversion: extrudes and textures models based on reference 2D images.
Automatic UV unwrapping: generates optimized UV layouts for AI-generated textures.
Format export: supports exporting assets to standard formats like GLTF and OBJ.
Pipeline integration: provides APIs for embedding generation capabilities into other tools.

useCases.title: Game Asset Creation
useCases.description: Rapidly prototype 3D props and environments for game development.

useCases.title: Virtual Reality
useCases.description: Generate optimized assets for immersive VR experiences.

useCases.title: Concept Art
useCases.description: Quickly visualize 2D concepts in three dimensions.

useCases.title: Synthetic Data
useCases.description: Produce varied 3D models for training computer vision systems.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Technical artists, game developers, and researchers exploring AI in 3D pipelines. It requires a capable GPU for local generation tasks.
